asw.name: auto-sea-way
asw.network: Generated from OpenStreetMap land polygons: 39 million H3 cells
asw.install: Docker image, or a binary plus the planet graph file
asw.settings: asw serve, GET /route?from=lat,lon&to=lat,lon&shore_buffer=1.0 (canals open, Arctic routes closed). shore_buffer is not the default; the other routers have no such option and ran with their defaults
asw.size: 1.43 GB graph (538 MB download) and a 10 MB binary
asw.memory: 409 MB resident on macOS after the test (the graph is memory-mapped; about 1.4 GB on Linux with the whole file in cache)
asw.time_note: Measured over HTTP on the same machine. The HTTP round trip took 0.2 ms.

searoute-py.name: searoute-py
searoute-py.settings: searoute(origin, destination, units='naut', append_orig_dest=True), default restrictions (Northwest Passage closed)
searoute-py.memory: 373 MB peak for the Python process
searoute-py.time_note: Measured in the same Python process.

scgraph.name: scgraph
scgraph.settings: GeoGraph.load_geograph('marnet').get_shortest_path(origin, destination), defaults otherwise. It has no option to close the Arctic routes.
scgraph.size: 1.3 MB package and a 0.8 MB network file
scgraph.memory: 66 MB peak for the Python process
scgraph.time_note: Measured in the same Python process.

searoute-ts.name: searoute-ts
searoute-ts.network: MARNET 20 km (Eurostat), the finest network in the package
searoute-ts.settings: seaRoute(origin, destination, {network: marnet-20km, appendOriginDestination: true, units: 'nauticalmiles'})
searoute-ts.memory: 248 MB peak for the Node.js process
searoute-ts.time_note: Measured in the same Node.js process.

eurostat.name: eurostat/searoute
eurostat.settings: java -jar searoute-jar-3.6.jar -res 5 -kiel 1 -corinth 1 (Kiel and Corinth canals opened to match auto-sea-way; other passages at their defaults)
eurostat.memory: 373 MB peak for the Java process
eurostat.time_note: The jar runs a batch of routes. All 45 routes took 9 to 20 s in three runs, and one route alone 1.4 s, most of it Java start-up and network loading.

arcnautical.name: @arcnautical/maritime-routing
arcnautical.network: 0.05° ocean grid from OpenStreetMap water polygons (about 5.5 km), with forced cells for narrow passages
arcnautical.settings: findOceanPath(fromLat, fromLon, toLat, toLon), the API for coordinates, with the defaults. Its port API (computeRoute) takes only UN/LOCODE port codes, so it cannot route between our coordinates.
arcnautical.size: 0.6 MB installed (590 KB unpacked, as npm reports it; the planet grid is a 106 KB file), no dependencies
arcnautical.memory: 369 to 700 MB peak for the Node.js process (three runs)
arcnautical.time_note: Measured in the same Node.js process on 6 November 2026, with its route cache cleared before every call.
